evidence_quotes: 70 earthquakes were recorded over the 14-day window, averaging 5 events per day
notable activity spikes on Feb 3 (9 events) and Feb 14 (9 events)
Nikolski, Alaska and Tobelo, Indonesia led all regions with 8 events each
Mohr, Iran and La Tirana, Chile (6 each)
Mohr, Iran (M4.1 at 1.9 km, M4.9 at 8.5 km), Tual, Indonesia (M4.8 at 2.0 km), and off Honshu, Japan (M5.2 at 2.7 km)
No tsunami warnings were triggered across any of the 30 sampled events
any event exceeding M6.5 in these zones should trigger immediate reassessment
criticisms: The report states 'averaging 5 events per day' — the digest shows 70 events over 14 days = exactly 5.0/day, so this is technically correct but the daily_counts only cover 14 days (Feb 2–15), which checks out.

The report references '30 sampled events' for the tsunami claim. The digest provides exactly 30 sample_events, so this is traceable, though the digest does not explicitly label the sample size as 30 — it is derivable by counting.
The late-period uptick claim of 'Feb 13–15 combined: 22 events' is verifiable: Feb 13=7, Feb 14=9, Feb 15=6 = 22. This is correct and traceable.

The M6.5 threshold mentioned in the monitoring recommendation ('any event exceeding M6.5') is not derived from the digest — it is an editorial judgment. However, this is framed as a forward-looking monitoring threshold, not a factual claim about past data, so it does not constitute a factual error.

The report says the Banda Sea event (M5.6) and Tobelo (M5.7) triggered no tsunami 'likely due to their intermediate-to-deep focal depths' — the depths (176.6 km and 152.9 km respectively) are in the digest and support this characterization.

The phrase 'broad, simultaneous fault-system stress' is an interpretive editorial claim not directly supported by the digest, but it is not a concrete factual assertion about numbers, places, or metadata.

The report does not explicitly state the M6.1 event's location or depth, which is prudent since the digest does not identify which sample event corresponds to the maximum magnitude — no fabrication here.
